refactor.description: Refactor code for clarity and performance
refactor.template:
Refactor only the requested code while preserving observable behavior and public interfaces unless a change is explicitly requested. Prefer existing helpers and simpler code; avoid speculative abstractions. Run focused checks and explain the material changes.
$ARGUMENTS

explain.template:
Explain the requested code using its actual callers and data flow. Start with its purpose, then cover the details relevant to the question. Use file references and a small example where useful; scale depth to the request.
$ARGUMENTS

deps.template:
Audit project dependencies for outdated versions, known vulnerabilities, and unused or duplicate packages. Use the existing lockfile and package manager. Report evidence and recommended changes; do not upgrade packages.
$ARGUMENTS

clean.template:
Inspect build artifacts, caches, and ignored files relevant to: $ARGUMENTS
List exact cleanup targets and use a dry run where available. Preserve source, credentials, user data, and unfamiliar files. Obtain approval for concrete destructive targets unless the user already explicitly authorized those targets; then execute and verify.

scaffold.template: Create a new $ARGUMENTS following the project’s existing conventions. Add meaningful tests where the behavior warrants them and verify the result.

learn.template:
Explain in depth (for someone with systems programming experience): $ARGUMENTS

Include: core concepts, how it works under the hood, use cases, pitfalls, code examples, resources.

diagram.template:
Generate a Mermaid diagram for: $ARGUMENTS

Choose the best diagram type (flowchart, sequence, class, ER, state, graph, gantt, gitGraph). Read relevant code first.

test.template:
Add or run the smallest useful tests for: $ARGUMENTS
Follow existing test conventions and check observable behavior, important boundaries, and realistic failure cases. For a bug, show the regression test catches the original behavior when feasible. Run focused checks, investigate failures, and report validation limits.

commit.description: Stage changes and craft a commit message
commit.template:
Review the current diff and Git status, select only files relevant to the requested change, and create a conventional commit. This command authorizes the commit; do not ask again unless the intended scope is ambiguous. Never amend or push unless explicitly requested.
$ARGUMENTS

review.description: Review code for bugs, security, and best practices
review.template:
Review the requested changes without editing: $ARGUMENTS
If no scope is given, inspect staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked changes. Trace affected callers and report actionable correctness, security, or regression findings with severity, file:line, triggering conditions, impact, and a concise fix. Lead with findings; do not invent issues or demand stylistic rewrites.

perf.template: Analyze for performance issues, measure, optimize, and re-measure: $ARGUMENTS

security.template:
Review the security of: $ARGUMENTS
Inspect the relevant trust boundaries and trace untrusted input to sensitive operations. Report evidenced vulnerabilities and prerequisites; distinguish confirmed issues from hypotheses. Keep the review read-only and do not probe live targets or access secrets.

docker.template:
Analyze or create Docker configuration for: $ARGUMENTS

Follow Docker best practices from the devops agent instructions.

migrate.template: Plan and execute migration with rollback strategy: $ARGUMENTS

explore.template:
Explore and map: $ARGUMENTS

Provide a concise summary suitable for onboarding.

verify.template:
Independently verify recent changes: $ARGUMENTS

Report findings honestly with evidence.

architect.template:
Design architecture for: $ARGUMENTS

Follow the output structure in your agent instructions.

debug.description: Systematically find and fix a bug
debug.template:
Debug: $ARGUMENTS

Follow the debugging methodology in your agent instructions.

write.description: Write text in your personal style

pdf.template:
Read and analyse: $ARGUMENTS
Use the PDF-capable read tool or pdftotext for extraction. Inspect rendered pages when charts, scans, or layout matter. Cite page numbers and distinguish extracted content from inference; do not interpret PDF bytes as plain text.

fix.description: Fix lint, type, and formatting errors
fix.template:
Fix all lint, type, and formatting errors: $ARGUMENTS

Fix at root cause, don't suppress. Re-run to verify.

plan.description: Think through a problem before implementing
plan.template:
Investigate and produce an actionable plan for: $ARGUMENTS
Resolve discoverable facts from the project first; ask about consequential missing requirements or tradeoffs. Include the behavior and acceptance criteria, implementation approach, compatibility or rollout concerns when relevant, and validation. State assumptions, keep scope proportional, and do not implement.

pr.template:
Create a PR for the current branch: $ARGUMENTS

Return the PR URL.

todo.description: Find TODOs, FIXMEs, HACKs in codebase
todo.template:
Find all TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX comments in source files (exclude node_modules, .git, build artifacts). Group by severity.
$ARGUMENTS

env.template:
Check dev environment health: tools, dependencies, configs, build.
$ARGUMENTS

mtg.description: Build, analyze, or optimize a Commander/EDH deck
mtg.template:
$ARGUMENTS
Use the relevant live-data helpers. Follow the full deck workflow only for deck-building requests.

new-project.template:
Initialize a new project: $ARGUMENTS

Ask if language/framework unclear. Set up standard tooling, .gitignore, README. Verify it builds.

research.description: Research a question using primary sources
research.template:
Research: $ARGUMENTS
Use primary sources, cite supporting links, and distinguish verified facts from inference.

frontend.template:
Implement: $ARGUMENTS
Follow existing UI patterns, verify keyboard accessibility and responsive behavior.
